title: Adding Asset Information on a Requisition
body:
Adding Asset Information on a Requisition

If you're an asset manager, use this procedure to enter asset information for the asset line items on a requisition on the Asset Workbench.

Prerequisites

  • You must have membership of the Asset Manager group to be able to access the Asset Workbench and enter asset information to the asset items on a requisition.

  • If you require to group together a main asset and one or more sub-assets to assign related asset values, you must create an asset group in which you bundle those items as related items. For more information about creating groups, see Creating Asset Groups.

  • If a line item on a requisition has multiple quantities, by default the buying solution assigns the same asset number to all units of that item. For example, if a line item on a requisition consists of 10 chairs, the buying solution assigns the same asset value to all 10 chairs. If you require each item to be tracked as a separate asset, you can choose to split a line into the required number of lines to ensure that the buying solution assigns unique asset values to each of those items.

Context

After you assign asset information to items on a requisition, asset records are created. The buying solution assigns asset values to the line items on the requisition based on the asset records.

Procedure

  1. From the guided buying home page, open the Asset Workbench tab, as shown in the following figure.

  2. From the Asset Workbench page, choose Manage for the appropriate requisition, as shown in the following figure.

  3. If required, choose Request View to display the details of the line items on the associated requisition.
  4. Perform one of the following actions:
    1. Specify the asset class, asset line type, and description for each asset.
    2. To specify the same values for asset class and asset line type for multiple line items, click Mass Edit and specify the appropriate values on the Mass Edit view. Select the appropriate line items to which the values must be applied and click OK.
  5. If you need to assign unique asset values to each item with multiple quantities, perform the following steps to split the quantity:
    1. Choose the more options icon () next to the item and choose Split.
    2. Enter a numeric value under the Lines column on the Split page to specify the number of independent lines you want to create.
    3. Choose Split.

      The line is split into multiple lines based on the specified value.

    4. Choose Done to return to the previous page.
  6. If required, create asset groups. For more information about creating asset groups, see Creating Asset Groups.
  7. Choose Finish.

    The buying solution sends a copy of the requisition to SAP ERP and adds asset values received from SAP ERP to the line items on the requisition.

  8. Choose Done to return to the Asset Workbench page.

Results

  • The requisition moves to the In Progress tab on your dashboard in guided buying. During this stage, you cannot edit, withdraw, or deny the requisition. The requisition moves to the Completed tab after asset values assigned (asset class and asset line type) to line items are approved. Asset values are automatically assigned when line items are approved.
